_comment: Tileable material prompts, derived from docs/WORLD.md section 8.3 and constrained by the rules in 8.4.
_token_budget: CLIP TRUNCATES AT 77 TOKENS AND DISCARDS THE REST SILENTLY. The 2026-08-21 smoke test ran at 126 tokens, so a third of every prompt -- including the whole anti-shadow clause, which sat at the tail -- never reached the model. That is why both outputs came back with baked directional shadows. Full prompt is 'zone_style + material prompt', in that order, so the lighting instructions sit at the FRONT and survive truncation. Keep the total under 77. tile.py counts tokens and warns before generating anything.
_lighting_note: A game albedo map must be flat and unlit -- the engine lights it at runtime, so painted-in shadows double up and read wrong from every angle. 'no shadows, flat even light, albedo' is load-bearing. Do not trim it.
_palette_note: NO PALETTE TINT IN zone_style. Second smoke test 2026-08-21 put 'amber and verdigris tint' in the shared style and it overwhelmed material identity -- the mine rock face came back as decorative turquoise stone. You tint a scene with LIGHTS, not with albedo maps: bake amber into every texture and you can never light it differently, and it all goes muddy. Albedo stays neutral; Marrow's sodium lamps do the palette work in-engine. Colour belongs only to materials that genuinely have it (copper is verdigris, rust is orange, concrete is grey).
_order_note: Material description leads, style follows. Total is ~30 tokens so nothing truncates and order is purely about emphasis -- and identity matters more than style.
_flat_note: NEVER use the word 'flat' in a prompt. Third smoke test 2026-08-21 used 'flat lay albedo, flat even light' meaning flat LIGHTING, and SDXL read it as flat DESIGN -- riveted steel came back as vector art in stained-glass shapes. 'Photograph' and 'diffuse even lighting' say the same thing with no second meaning.
